common.title: JobLume
common.subtitle: A career database with job-description matching
common.description: JobLume keeps your experience in a reusable career database, then checks every requirement in a job description against it, with a rank and a coverage verdict. The AI judges but never writes your content. No account, all data stays in your browser, export to PDF or back up as JSON.

hero.subtitle: Your career database is the single source of truth. Paste a job description and every requirement is checked against your experience, with a rank and a coverage verdict you can open and inspect.

features.title: Three things, each closer to the application
features.subtitle: From tidying your experience to cutting it down for a specific role — all inside your own browser.

card1.title: Career database
card1.desc: Maintain it once, reuse it everywhere. Education, work, projects and skills each in their place, picked per resume.

card2.title: Requirement by requirement
card2.desc: A job description is broken into hard requirements, nice-to-haves and duties — each one pointing at the experience behind it, instead of an unexplainable score.

card3.title: The AI only judges
card3.desc: No rewriting, no ghostwriting. The model classifies and matches; there is no code path that edits your words.

templates.title: Four templates, and that is enough
templates.subtitle: Every one exports a real text layer — not an image. Selectable and copyable.

point1.title: You do the selecting
point1.desc: Nothing is pre-checked. Every line that reaches your resume is one you ticked yourself.

point2.title: Works without an API key
point2.desc: Without a key, the database, templates and exports all still work — you just lose the match annotations.

point3.title: Every judgement is checkable
point3.desc: A verdict must name the experience behind it, or it is downgraded; a quoted JD line that cannot be found is cleared.

cta.title: Start building your resume
cta.description: Your data lives in your own browser. Export to PDF, PNG, JSON or Markdown whenever you like.

footer.tagline: A personal job-hunting tool. Nothing is uploaded, no account needed.

faqDialog.description: Common tips and solutions for the JobLume workbench.

browser-compatibility.question: Which browser is recommended?
browser-compatibility.answer: We recommend using the latest version of Chrome or Edge for the best layout and export experience. Some outdated browsers may cause styling issues.

export-failure.question: What if export fails or style is broken?
export-failure.answer:
1. We recommend using Google Chrome (https://www.google.cn/intl/zh-CN/chrome/) for best compatibility.
2. If it still fails, try in 'Incognito Mode' to exclude extension interference.
3. Alternatively, click 'PDF (Backup)' in the export menu and select 'Save as PDF' in the print dialog.

export-methods.question: Which export format should I use?
export-methods.answer:
• PDF: Uses the browser print dialog to save a PDF. Real text layer, selectable and copyable — recommended for formal applications and printing. Note: in practice about 11% of Chinese characters come out distorted in ATS parsing; double-check before submitting.

• PDF (Long Page): Renders the resume as an image in a custom-height, single-page PDF. Best for online preview and sharing; not recommended for printing, text selection, or ATS parsing.

• PNG (Long Image): Exports the resume as one tall image. Best for mobile preview, portfolios, and image-upload workflows.

• JSON Config: Exports a resume data backup for restoration or migration.

• Markdown: Exports plain text for use in other tools.

drag-and-drop.question: How do I drag and drop to reorder modules?
drag-and-drop.answer: In the 'Layout' settings of the left edit panel, hover your cursor over the 'Drag Handle' (usually represented by a six-dot icon) on the left side of the module card. Click and hold the left mouse button to drag the module up or down to reorder the sections of your entire resume.

basic.birthDateNote: Day precision, stored back as YYYY/MM/DD.
